verdict.reasoning: Patient states symptoms for four days: "I've been feeling kind of under the weather for the past four days. It started with a sore throat and runny nose... It's sort of going into a cough now... Kind of bad and tired."
Patient reports painful swallowing for one day and improvement: "it was quite painful to swallow... For one of the days" and later says sore throat is "sort of going away."
Clear rhinorrhea and congestion are described: "runny nose" and "it's. It's clear" with "getting my nose stuffed all the time. It's very hard to get it free... you feel quite congested."
Onset and type of cough: "that started recently, like just maybe yesterday. And it's. It's dry for now."
Night sweats explicitly mentioned: "I forgot to mention that I'm also having night sweats."
Initial fever, now settling with medications: "I had some fever in the beginning, but it's now sort of going down. I've been taking some paracetamol and I Bupren for that and they help."
Exertional dyspnea only: "I feel a bit winded on exertion" and clarified "when you're resting, there's no problem?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah. When I'm resting, it's okay."
Chest pain denied: "In terms of your chest... any pain in your chest?" Patient: "So no pain in the chest."

Intermittent generalized headaches: "Any headaches at all?" – "Yeah, yeah, that's still there." "Whereabouts..." – "Just sort of general... they're not always there, but... every now and then they would come and go."
Decreased appetite: "How's your appetite, sir?" Patient: "Maybe a bit less than what I would usually have."
Increased fluid intake: "Yeah, I've been drinking a little bit more. More than the usual."
Nausea/vomiting denied: "any feeling of nausea or any vomiting?" Patient: "None of that."
Normal bowel and urinary habits: "Tell me about your bowels. Are your bowels working okay?" – "Yeah, yeah, I think so." "Passing urine okay?" – "Yeah, yeah."
Ear symptoms denied: "Any pain in your ears at all?" – "No." "You don't feel blocked or any discharge coming out of your ears?" – "I don't think so."
Rash denied: "Have you noticed any funny rashes at all on your skin?" Patient: "No. No."
Visual changes and photophobia denied: "any problems with your eyesight, your vision?" – "No." "Any difficulty with seeing bright lights?" – "No, I don't think so."

Sick contact at work with colleague whose kids are in kindergarten: "it all started with the colleague of mine. She just kept sneezing next to me all the time. I think her kids are catching something from the. From their kindergarten or something."

No past medical history: "Are you otherwise fitting well or do you have any other medical problems I should be aware of?" Patient: "So otherwise that I'm fine. There's. There isn't anything that I'm taking or I'm being treated for?"
Paracetamol use: "I've been taking some paracetamol... for that and they help."
Ibuprofen use: "I've been taking some paracetamol and I Bupren for that and they help" (ibuprofen referenced).
No drug allergies: "Any allergies at all to any medications." Patient: "...No."
Grandmother with type 2 diabetes: "Yeah, my grandma has diabetes." and later "I think it's type two."
Great-grandfather with eczema: "I think one of my great granddads had an eczema."
Living situation: "Tell me, who do you live with at home?" – "I live alone."
Employment as accountant and currently working: "And you said you're working at the moment, is that right?" – "Yeah, yeah." "What do you do for work?" – "I'm an accountant."

Increased work stress but coping: "it's a bit of a stressful period. Just around the end of the year." and later "No, I think, I think it's, it's the, you know, it's the good kind of stress... No, no, I, I, I like my job."
Occasional cigars: "in terms of smoking, do you smoke at all?" – "Yeah, occasionally. No cigars and things on company parties."
Occasional social alcohol: "And what about alcohol?" – "Occasionally, I would have some. I'm not a very big drinker." "Again, socially, with work."

Clinician assessment: "you probably have... a bit of a viral... upper respiratory tract infection or maybe early signs of a flu" plus four‑day course and listed symptoms (improving sore throat, runny nose, dry cough, initial fever, night sweats, muscle pain, weakness, headache, mild exertional breathlessness, no chest pain) all appear in the history and in the clinician’s summary.
Rest, fluids, 1–2 days off work: "get plenty of rest. I'll probably advise you taking a day or two of work if you can, making yourself, you know, pushing fluids and make yourself well hydrated."
Continue paracetamol and ibuprofen: "continuing with the regular paracetamol and ibuprofen, and we should see how things go."
Expected 7–10 day course: "It normally lasts for about seven to 10 days and just gets better, really, over time."
Follow up if not improving by next week: "If next week you're still better, I want you to come back and see me." (context clearly intends if not better next week to return).

Return sooner for red flags: "things to look out for. If you're really not getting better, if you have a high fever or your breathing is becoming a bit more labored, or chest pain, I'd like you to come back and see me much sooner." (worsening dyspnea and chest pain explicitly mentioned).
ROS negative for nausea/vomiting: "any feeling of nausea or any vomiting?" – "None of that."
ROS negative for ear pain/discharge: "Any pain in your ears at all?" – "No." and "any discharge coming out of your ears?" – "I don't think so."
ROS negative for rash: "Have you noticed any funny rashes at all on your skin?" – "No. No."
ROS negative for visual changes and photophobia: "any problems with your eyesight, your vision?" – "No." and "Any difficulty with seeing bright lights?" – "No, I don't think so."
